teams.heading: Fiji surrender Pacific Nations Cup title following narrow defeat in Tokyo
teams.body: The Flying Fijians surrendered their Pacific Nations Cup crown in Saturday's final, falling 20-15 to Japan in a tense Tokyo encounter. Despite first-half tries from Virimi Vakatawa and hooker Tevita Ikanivere, the defending champions struggled with discipline, losing Mesake Doge to a yellow card. Isaiah Armstrong-Ravula levelled the scores at 15-15 with a penalty in the final quarter, but Tongan-born Samisoni Tua crashed over with 10 minutes left to secure victory for Eddie Jones' side.

lead.why: Fiji's narrow defeat to Japan in the Pacific Nations Cup final on Saturday is the most significant sporting event of the weekend.

teams.heading: Jack van Poortvliet backs England to win the 2027 Rugby World Cup
teams.body: Scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet has declared that Steve Borthwick’s squad possesses the "100% capability of winning" the 2027 Rugby World Cup. After starting all three Nations Championship Tests during the summer, the 25-year-old revealed that his previous ankle injury allowed for a period of reflection and "new-found enjoyment" of the game. Van Poortvliet, who reclaimed the No. 9 shirt following Alex Mitchell’s hamstring issues, remains critical of his own form, stating he is not "anywhere near" his desired level despite England’s recent victories.

teams.heading: Jemima Adams Verling debuts as Ireland face USA in Tallaght Stadium
teams.body: Ireland begin a new three-year World Cup cycle today as they host the USA in the WXV Global Series at Tallaght Stadium. Head coach Scott Bemand has handed a senior debut to Connacht back row Jemima Adams Verling, who starts at blind-side flanker. With Sam Monaghan sidelined by an Achilles injury, Bemand described the series as a "turning of the page" to build squad depth. Ireland have won three consecutive meetings against the USA, most recently in 2024.

teams.heading: World Rugby's ambition to stage Six Nations match in USA stalls
teams.body: Plans to host a Six Nations fixture in the United States remain in limbo despite ongoing discussions led by World Rugby. Reports from earlier this month confirmed that while World Rugby is pushing the concept to expand the tournament's global reach, resistance persists among the unions. With major stakeholders like England expressing reluctance due to potential financial losses and other nations citing no current plans for such a move, a specific venue or confirmed date for the fixture remains elusive.

teams.heading: Wales Women crush South Africa as Sean Lynn hails new DNA
teams.body: Wales ended a nine-match winless streak in spectacular fashion, dismantling South Africa 50-19 at Cardiff Arms Park on Friday. Head coach Sean Lynn’s bold decision to shift scrum-half Keira Bevan to fly-half paid dividends as Wales ran in eight tries, with Sisilia Tuipulotu scoring a brace and co-captain Alex Callender earning player-of-the-match honours. Reflecting on the dominant performance, Lynn stated, "This is just the start for us, this is going to be our new DNA."

teams.heading: Eddie Jones’ Japan defeat Fiji to secure Pacific Nations Cup title
teams.body: Japan claimed the Pacific Nations Cup on Saturday, defeating Fiji 20-15 in a tense final in Tokyo. After falling short against the Flying Fijians in the previous two finals, the Brave Blossoms secured victory through a late try by Samisoni Tua. Ben Gunter and Mamoru Harada also crossed for the hosts in a match that remained in the balance until the final 10 minutes. The win provides a significant boost for Eddie Jones’ squad ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup cycle.

teams.heading: Black Ferns cruise to victory as New Zealand dismantle Scotland side
teams.body: The Black Ferns secured a dominant 66-14 victory against Scotland at Hive Stadium to open their WXV campaign. New Zealand established control early, with tries from Mo’omo’oga Palu and Maama Mo’onia Vaipulu setting the tempo. Despite two first-half scores from Evie Gallagher, the visitors’ attack proved unstoppable, running in 10 tries in total. Layla Sae and Amy Du Plessis helped extend the lead before half-time, ensuring a comfortable start to the tournament ahead of next Saturday's fixture against England.
